page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton family. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running on AWS Neoverse-N1 silicon at 2.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES instructions enabled. Operating on a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). It has no local storage bundled, relying on network-attached EBS volumes, and includes no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive parallel execution balanced by moderate single-thread compute capabilities. In stress-ng, the c6gn.2xlarge hits 1519.79 in single-core and scales linearly across dedicated cores to 12130.94 in multi-core testing. Memory performance reaches 472.59 GB/sec for small cached reads, 119.78 GB/sec for large uncached block reads, and 52.48 GB/sec for large writes. Application-level evaluations record 9.2 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 9.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Geekbench scores show 8571.0 for software compilation using Clang and 5435.0 in overall multi-core throughput, while single-core Geekbench settles at 946.0.

The primary tradeoffs are reflected in single-threaded bottlenecks, compression speeds, and synthetic cryptographic evaluation. PassMark registers a lower CPU score of 5203.69 and an encryption score of 1082.7, alongside weak compression metrics such as 20.35 GB/sec in single-thread gzip. LLM token generation rates range from 38.56 tokens per second on a 135M model to 6.78 tokens per second on a 7B model. Nonetheless, with 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and full physical core isolation without hyperthreading, the instance offers strong resource efficiency for clustered networking and horizontally scalable workloads like CI/CD compilation, distributed caching, web serving, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by 8 dedicated AWS Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a 1:2 compute profile, it pairs 8 vCPUs with 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no bundled local storage and contains no discrete graphics hardware. Benchmark results display solid multi-core throughput, recording 12130.94 in stress-ng multi-core, 8571.0 in Clang software compilation, and 9.2 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Conversely, single-thread metrics and data compression reflect modest performance levels, with single-core Geekbench scoring 946.0. Without hyperthreading or resource sharing, the c6gn.2xlarge delivers predictable execution and cost-efficient processing for microservices, web servers, code build pipelines, and networked caching layers.
